The largest gains are distinct electric aircraft propulsion, physical consequences of damage and ground contact, and start/stop/locking cues for machinery. Several requested continuous sounds already have assets and code; first confirm how they sound in the actual game.

Evidence boundary: existing coverage is based on current source and scene inspection, not a fresh game playback test. The 52 candidates were decoded and measured; I have not judged them by ear. Their proposed roles are source-based hypotheses, not final creative approvals. Use the playback cards to audition them.

1. Finish the audible machinery

Check the deck and island lift motors, track loops and carrier ambience at real listener positions. Add lift release, stop and locking clunks; catapult and recovery-robot events.

The current elevator helper now supplies valid WAV loop endpoints and the deck elevator retries stopped playback. Earlier silence reports should be re-tested rather than assumed current.

2. Give aircraft their own propulsion

Eight fixed-wing aircraft share airplane_propeller 3.wav. Crusader (2) and Dagger (7) share airplane_propeller 1.wav. All six helicopters share one three-speed rotor set.

Build motor tone + blade pulse + airflow layers, then assign identities and startup/coast-down envelopes. Pitch shifting one loop will not carry all the differences.

3. Make damage and landings physical

Regional damage and ground contact have useful code hooks, but no dedicated audio was found for part tear-off, damaged motors, sustained belly scraping or bouncing debris.

Use initial impact → sustained contact → secondary debris → settling. Surface, speed and part size should control the sound.

4. Repair a likely flap hookup gap

Ten numbered fixed-wing scenes assign FlapSoundLoop a plain Resource placeholder whose metadata names the missing Audio/flaps_deploy 2.wav. A separate Audio/flaps/flap_loop.ogg is present without a literal hookup.

This is static evidence of an assignment problem, not a newly reproduced runtime failure. It deserves an early targeted check.

Best first auditions

NeedStart withMeasured reason / practical caution
Electric aircraft motorsS01 electric motorcycle, S02 long motor, S07 electromagnetic rotary toolS01's selected 8-second region has about 3 dB envelope spread. S02 has about 92% of measured energy above 2 kHz: a whine layer, not enough low body alone. S07 is extremely steady and mid-dominant; use as a designed electrical accent.
Propeller air beatingS08 PropSmoothExt, S10 PropHummerSlow, S12 helicopter bladesS08/S10 are dominated by 20–200 Hz energy and have steady envelopes, useful complements to brighter motor layers. They are only 2–3 seconds long; repetition must be checked.
Carrier / cockpit room textureS16 ventilation fan, S19 lighthouse motor roomThe fan is already a source for installed mixes. Lighthouse motor room provides a longer electrical machinery alternative with more midrange energy; avoid copying its full 96 seconds into a positional effect.
Elevators and locksS24 elevator loop, S26 heavy mechanism, S28 bolt latch, S29 bolt handlingTravel loops have relatively steady envelopes. The latch candidates are transients with roughly 24 dB crest factors; layer a heavier body hit for deck-elevator scale. S28's raw recording is quiet.
Carrier tracksS31 tread A, S32 tread B, S34 installed derivativeA/B provide 14–15 seconds of source and are strongly low-frequency dominated. The existing filtered derivative is already available; add texture/transition cues after checking its mix.
Airframe break and crash slideS37 metal friction, S38 debris, S40 chassis impact, S42 concrete scrapeThese are components of a designed event, not complete airplane sounds. S35 scrape is only 1.19 seconds and has a 40 dB envelope spread: reject it as a direct continuous slide loop.
Replicator and robot armsS46 robot servo, S48 3D-printer servoGesture/sequence recordings should be split to match actual arm movement; do not run the entire recording continuously.

Production order

  1. Verify and repair current coverage: elevator/track audibility, flap stream assignments, unused shutdown asset, cockpit/wind overlap.
  2. Add missing physical feedback: elevator locks, touchdown/crash slides, part breakaway, damaged motor, catapult/catch, recovery clamps.
  3. Build vehicle identity: start with two contrasting aircraft and light/heavy helicopters, then apply per-aircraft profiles across the full fleet.
  4. Expand the world: room zones, ground vehicles, harvester, replicator, electrical storms and sparse location ambience.

Implementation acceptance checks

Preserve separate motor and aerodynamic layers; use modest pitch ranges with state crossfades. Drive scrape from sustained contact and relative speed, damage transients from actual detach events, and locks from final aligned state. Use variation without adjacent repeats, bounded one-shot pools and distance budgets. Prioritize cockpit warnings and radio over ambience.

Check output from cockpit, external view, commander interior, open deck and beside each mechanism. Verify pause, ejection, destruction, stopping and leaving range silence the right sources. Measure actual mixer output as well as player state; a node or valid WAV alone does not prove the player hears it.

Scope, method and reproducibility

Recursive disk inventory covers D:\Game audio, D:\Downloads\Soniss and this project's Audio folder. It is not a scan of every drive, compressed archive or cloud folder. Counts are files, not unique sounds; no content hashing/deduplication was performed. Mono/stereo counterparts, raw sources and derivatives can overlap.

52 sources were probed with ffprobe. Sources up to 36 seconds were fully decoded; longer sources were sampled at 0%, 35% and 70% for up to 16 seconds each. Metrics are on decoded/resampled 24 kHz stereo samples, not original-rate true peaks or LUFS. A relatively steady audible region was chosen for loop candidates; an energetic region for events. A quiet steady window can be background noise, so verify by ear.

Previews are up to 10 seconds, gain-adjusted toward −4 dBFS peak with gain capped at +12 dB, and given 10 ms edge fades. They are not loudness matched, edited production loops, or recordings of the game mix. The spectral bars show 20 Hz and above; unfilled remainder is below 20 Hz, including DC. Original start offsets and all metrics are retained in candidate_analysis.json. Nothing was uploaded.

Reproduce with python inventory.py, python refine_inventory.py, python analyze_candidates.py, then python build_report.py from this folder. Full scan can take several minutes on the source drive. The source list used by analysis is saved in all_paths.txt.

What the game already contains

1,086 files / 409.49 MB: 115 effects, 1 music track, 470 files in runtime voice folders, and 500 archived voice-source files. 85 non-voice files have literal or verified formatted code/scene references, including music; 31 have no literal reference found. A reference is not a guarantee of live use. Runtime voices are discovered dynamically, and folder membership does not guarantee every phrase is selected.

Potentially useful unassigned files include propeller slowing down.wav, flap_loop.ogg, alternate rotor files, several propeller loops and legacy carrier recordings. Retain them during review; “no reference found” is not permission to delete.

Aircraft sound identities

Creative targets for all 16 numbered aircraft, grounded in the current vehicle catalog. These are proposals, not analyzed final mixes. Keep source variants and filters consistent within a family while varying actual motor, pulse and load response.

The current catalog describes Razorback (6) as a turboprop. Your request favors electric engines; the proposed audio direction follows that request, but the catalog wording needs reconciliation before implementation.

Be selective

Combustion aircraft/tank recordings can contaminate an electric vehicle identity. “Metal Tensions” in the 2024 Rogue Waves pack is guitar material, not structural metal fracture. Electromagnetic pickups are designed layers, not ordinary acoustic recordings.

Up to 150 matching rows shown; refine search for more precise results. Duration and audio format are header metadata, not proof of sound quality.
